items.sourceText: Trump’s Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy Yanks 133 Illegal Electronic Logging Devices from Trucking Registry to Protect American Truckers, Fight Fraud Thursday, November 12, 2026 Historic crackdown is the largest ELD revocation in FMCSA history WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy today announced the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA) pulled 133 illegal Electronic Logging Devices (ELDs) from the agency’s Registered Devices List in its latest effort to stop fraud, protect American truckers, and safeguard America’s roads. This historic crackdown targeted illegal logging devices used by fraudsters to cheat safety rules, bypass mandated rest periods, and undercut trucker wages. The use of these illegal logging devices can be directly sourced to deadly crashes across America. Image Click HERE to learn how fraudulent ELDs put American drivers at risk The instances of fraud and abuse were severe and endangered thousands of Americans on our roads. Examples include (cases are anonymized to avoid compromising ongoing investigations) : ELD Company A allowed carriers to completely bypass hours of service limits by calling a support line to manually wipe out driving time and fabricate rest periods while actively driving. ELD Company B was caught actively uploading fake logs during an active roadside inspection to cover up an overworked driver operating hours beyond the legal limit. ELD Company C logs showed drivers traveling at mathematically impossible speeds of up to 130 miles per hour to compress driving time. “Under President Trump’s leadership, we are cracking down on rampant fraud on America’s roads. This latest crackdown – which required hundreds of man hours and extensive forensic investigations – will prevent criminals from cooking the books, sabotaging trucker wages, and endangering you and your family when you drive,” said U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy. “From pulling thousands of illegal licenses to shutting down sham schools to launching our Freedom Haulers campaign, our message is simple: America’s roads are for American truckers. This administration will stop at nothing to protect the driving public.” Federal hours-of-service limits prevent driver fatigue and save lives. When non-compliant or manipulated ELDs allow carriers to falsify driving logs, exhausted drivers remain behind the wheel far beyond safe, legal limits. They can also depress wages by allowing companies to offer cheaper rates. Today’s action removes 121 agency-revoked devices and 12 voluntary self-revocations that failed to meet the Trump Administration’s standards of readiness. “Motor carriers must have confidence that every device on FMCSA’s public registry is compliant, secure, and actively supported,” said FMCSA Administrator Derek D. Barrs. "We are removing noncompliant and fraudulent devices to close loopholes that can be exploited to evade oversight, avoid revocation, bypass vetting requirements, or undermine accurate hours-of-service records. This action protects law-abiding carriers and drivers and makes clear that FMCSA will not tolerate devices that compromise the integrity of the ELD system.” Since President Trump issued an Executive Order to restore integrity to the trucking industry in April 2025, Secretary Duffy and FMCSA have: Placed 34,000 drivers out of service who could not speak basic English or read road signs; Shut down nearly 10,000 driving schools; and Revoked more than 31,000 illegally issued licenses to unvetted foreign drivers. Additional Information: ELDs are used by truck drivers and carriers to record hours-of-service information. ELDs track driving time and other critical information, making it easier to accurately record, manage, and share required hours-of-service data. FMCSA maintains a public list of ELDs that providers have registered and self-certified as compliant with federal requirements. Motor carriers have up to 60 days to replace the revoked ELDs with a compliant ELD. For more information on ELDs and to find a list of the revoked devices, visit FMCSA’s ELD website . After 60 days, motor carriers who continue to use the revoked devices will be considered as operating without an ELD. Safety officials who encounter a driver using the revoked devices on or after November 24, 2026, should cite 395.8(a)(1) and place the driver out-of-service (OOS) in accordance with the Commercial Vehicle Safety Alliance OOS Criteria . If the ELD provider corrects all identified deficiencies for its device, FMCSA will place the ELD back on the list of registered devices and inform the industry of the update. ###

items.summary: WASHINGTON, D.C. – The Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA) has launched the enhanced FMCSA Complaint Center, providing a more streamlined way to report potential violations of federal motor carrier safety and hazardous materials regulations. This effort is part of the U.S. Department of Transportation’s Pro-Trucker Package unveiled in June 20
items.sourceText: FMCSA Enhances Complaint Center to Strengthen Trucking Safety and Accountability Friday, November 6, 2026 INFORMATION BULLETIN Contact: FMCSA.PublicAffairs@dot.gov New Platform Makes It Easier for Drivers, Industry Professionals, and the Public to Report Safety and Compliance Concerns WASHINGTON, D.C. – The Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA) has launched the enhanced FMCSA Complaint Center, providing a more streamlined way to report potential violations of federal motor carrier safety and hazardous materials regulations. This effort is part of the U.S. Department of Transportation’s Pro-Trucker Package unveiled in June 2025 by Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy in support of President Donald Trump’s Executive Order 14286 , Enforcing Commonsense Rules of the Road for America’s Truck Drivers . The FMCSA Complaint Center provides an accessible channel for reporting potential safety and compliance concerns across the commercial motor vehicle industry. By making it easier to share critical information, FMCSA can better identify potential threats, hold unsafe operators and bad actors accountable, and advance its mission to reduce crashes, injuries, and fatalities involving large trucks and buses. Formerly known as the National Consumer Complaint Database (NCCDB), the FMCSA Complaint Center has undergone significant improvements since the updated system launched last year. Recent enhancements include: Expanded complaint categories: New categories cover property brokers, Entry-Level Driver Training/Training Provider Registry (ELDT/TPR), intermodal equipment providers, and registration-related fraud and identity theft. Updated name and audience references: The latest release renames the platform the FMCSA Complaint Center and replaces references to “consumer” with “general public” to better reflect the range of individuals who can submit complaints. Improved user experience: FMCSA has overhauled the website and complaint submission form and updated the complaint search tool to make the platform easier to navigate. Reorganized categories: The Medical Review Officer/Substance Abuse Professionals category is now included under a new category, Drug and Alcohol Service Agents. How to Submit a Complaint FMCSA encourages individuals who witness a potential violation to submit a complaint as soon as possible. Complainants do not need to have every detail before filing and should provide the information available to them. FMCSA reviews complaints alongside other information to determine which companies or regulated entities may warrant further review, investigation, or enforcement action. Submitting a complaint does not automatically trigger an investigation or result in a violation or penalty. Online: complaint.fmcsa.dot.gov By phone: 1-888-DOT-SAFT (1-888-368-7238), 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. Eastern Time, Monday through Friday. Eligible complaints: www.fmcsa.dot.gov/complaint-center/eligible-complaints For emergencies or situations requiring immediate attention, call 911. ###

items.title: OPERATION HIGHWAY SHIELD: Trump’s Transportation Department Yanks More Than 300 Dangerous Truckers, Illegals off U.S. Roads
items.summary: LITTLE ROCK, AR — U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy today announced the results of the third wave of Operation Highway Shield, a Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA)-led, multiagency operation targeting unqualified big rig drivers and criminal activity on American roads.
items.sourceText: OPERATION HIGHWAY SHIELD: Trump’s Transportation Department Yanks More Than 300 Dangerous Truckers, Illegals off U.S. Roads Wednesday, November 4, 2026 Third wave of multiagency operation conducted 1,724 inspections in 48 hours in Arkansas LITTLE ROCK, AR — U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy today announced the results of the third wave of Operation Highway Shield, a Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA)-led, multiagency operation targeting unqualified big rig drivers and criminal activity on American roads. FMCSA inspectors partnered with Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), Immigration & Customs Enforcement (ICE), the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), and the Arkansas Highway Police for a 48-hour operation to crack down on unsafe drivers, hazardous vehicles, and fraudulent practices along Arkansas highways and major freight corridors. The operation resulted in: 393 drivers and vehicles placed out of service 183 English Language Proficiency (ELP) violations 74 immigration violations referred for federal immigrations enforcement 44 criminal arrests 1 stolen trailer recovered “Gone are the days of dangerous–and many times illegal and foreign–drivers putting American lives at risk on our roads. Under the Trump Administration, we are restoring law and order,” said U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy. “This latest wave of Operation Highway Shield has pulled over 300 dangerous drivers off the road including 183 foreign drivers that couldn't read road signs. We are not slowing down when it comes to keeping Americans safe on our roads.” “Every person on the road deserves to get home safely,” said FMCSA Administrator Derek D. Barrs. “When criminal activity and unsafe vehicles creep onto our highways, it puts everyone at risk. Operation Highway Shield is about teaming up with our partners to protect everyday drivers, clear out the bad actors, and make our roads safer for everyone.” The first wave of Operation Highway Shield resulted in 176 drivers being taken out of service, 54 of which were taken out of service for language deficiencies. Additionally, 35 individuals were arrested on criminal-related charges, and 42 individuals were taken into custody for violating federal immigration laws. The second wave was conducted in Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, and Ohio, resulting in 51 illegal immigrants detained, 766 unsafe drivers and vehicles placed out of service, 36 English Language Proficiency test violations, and $1 million of stolen cargo recovered. Additional Information: In August, USDOT, the Department of Homeland Security, the Department of Justice, and the White House Task Force to Eliminate Fraud teamed up to launch a historic interagency effort to crack down on fraud in the trucking industry. As part of the crackdown, FMCSA carried out the emergency removal of 110 commercial driver’s license (CDL) schools associated with more than 5,000 drivers who failed English language proficiency tests and put 160 more schools on notice. Since President Trump issued the Executive Order to restore integrity to the trucking industry in April 2025, Secretary Duffy has: Knocked 33,000 drivers out of service who could not speak basic English or read road signs Revoked 31,000 illegally issued licenses to unvetted foreign drivers and Shut down nearly 10,000 shady driving schools ###

items.sourceText: FMCSA Announces Funding Opportunity to Support Crash Causal Factors Program Heavy-Duty Truck Study Tuesday, November 3, 2026 INFORMATION BULLETIN Contact: FMCSA.PublicAffairs@dot.gov Up to $7 million available in one-time competitive funding to support crash data collection for the CCFP Heavy-Duty Truck Study. WASHINGTON, DC – The U.S. Department of Transportation’s (USDOT) Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA) is now accepting applications for the Crash Causal Factors Program (CCFP) Cooperative Agreement Program. The funding opportunity will support activities that maximize effective data collection in support of the CCFP Heavy-Duty Truck Study, which will examine fatal crashes involving heavy-duty trucks to better understand the factors contributing to these crashes. The CCFP Cooperative Agreement Program will award up to $7 million in total funding, with no single award exceeding $500,000. This is the only funding opportunity that will be offered in support of the study, and awards are intended to support the duration of the data collection period. Eligible Activities and Costs Funding may be used for activities and equipment that directly support data collection on qualifying crashes within the study’s sampling locations, including: Post-crash commercial motor vehicle (CMV) inspections Crash reconstructions Post-crash investigations Crash data reporting Equipment needed for data collection Qualifying crashes involve fatalities and Class 7 or 8 heavy-duty trucks. All expenses must directly support data collection on qualifying crashes within the study’s designated sampling locations. Please refer to the NOFO for additional details and limitations. Funding Eligibility States selected to participate in the CCFP Heavy-Duty Truck Study, designated alternate States, as well as local law enforcement agencies that meet the study’s participation requirements, are eligible to apply. The funding will be made available through a cooperative agreement. Application Information and Key Dates Application Deadline: Applications may be submitted through December 28, 2026. Funding Educational Webinar: A prerecorded webinar is available [ here ]. Office Hours: Join a virtual session to have your questions answered on Thursday, November 12, 11am─12pm EST ( registration required ). Agencies are encouraged to share this funding opportunity with their grant management teams and personnel responsible for preparing applications. Agencies that partner with other organizations on crash data collection for the study should also ensure those partners are aware of the opportunity. Additional Information The CCFP is part of USDOT and FMCSA’s effort to reduce roadway fatalities involving commercial motor vehicles (CMVs) and aims to strengthen the scientific understanding of CMV-involved crashes through a series of peer-reviewed studies, a national crash data repository, and ongoing analysis. The findings and anonymized data will help government agencies, State and local partners, researchers, safety advocacy groups and other stakeholders improve safety programs and develop effective crash countermeasures. State and local partners will play a critical role in collecting and submitting crash data to support the program’s research. Applicants must identify performance goals and indicators demonstrating how their proposed activities will support data collection and reporting, post-crash CMV inspections, and post-crash investigations and/or crash reconstructions involving qualifying crashes. Applicants should review the Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) on Grants.gov for complete eligibility requirements, application instructions and submission details. To learn more about the CCFP Heavy-Duty Truck Study, visit FMCSA’s CCFP webpage .

items.title: FMCSA Announces All 50 States Have Implemented Reformed DataQs Review Process, Enhancing Due Process and Improving Timeliness for Drivers
items.summary: WASHINGTON, DC - The U.S. Department of Transportation’s (USDOT) Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA) today officially announced the implementation of updated requirements for the DataQs review process, giving truck drivers and motor carriers a clearer, fairer and more timely way to challenge safety information they believe is inaccurate.
items.sourceText: FMCSA Announces All 50 States Have Implemented Reformed DataQs Review Process, Enhancing Due Process and Improving Timeliness for Drivers Friday, October 16, 2026 INFORMATION BULLETIN Contact: FMCSA.PublicAffairs@dot.gov All 50 states, Washington, D.C., and U.S. territories now meet updated requirements for a standardized, multi-level review process, improving fairness for America’s truck drivers. WASHINGTON, DC - The U.S. Department of Transportation’s (USDOT) Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA) today officially announced the implementation of updated requirements for the DataQs review process, giving truck drivers and motor carriers a clearer, fairer and more timely way to challenge safety information they believe is inaccurate. “Truck drivers and motor carriers deserve a fair and clear process when they believe their safety record contains inaccurate information,” said FMCSA Administrator Derek D. Barrs . “We promised the trucking industry that we would strengthen the DataQs process by improving timeliness and enhancing due process, and we are delivering. These changes give drivers and carriers a clearer path to challenge inaccurate data, understand where their request stands, and receive a timely decision.” Improving DataQs was a commitment in Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy’s Pro-Trucker Package, announced in summer 2025, following President Trump’s Executive Order aimed at improving working conditions for America’s truck drivers With these changes now in place nationwide, USDOT and FMCSA are delivering on that commitment and strengthening due process for the men and women who keep America’s economy moving. What’s changing in DataQs The revised requirements establish a more streamlined framework for handling Requests for Data Review (RDRs), specifically for states and U.S. territories receiving Motor Carrier Safety Assistance Program (MCSAP) funding from FMCSA. General Requirements States must designate points of contact for crash and inspection RDRs. States are required to review requests submitted within three years of an inspection and within five years of a crash. All decisions, especially those where no data correction is made, must include detailed explanations, evidence reviewed, and clear next steps in the review process. States must participate in FMCSA program reviews and follow established policies, including those related to adjudicated citations. Three-Stage Review Process: States must implement a multi-stage, independent review structure that includes: Initial Review – Ensures decisions are not made solely by the issuing officer when denying a correction. Reconsideration – Conducted by independent subject matter experts not involved in the initial decision. Final Review – Completed by a senior decision-maker or independent panel, ensuring an unbiased final determination. Timeline Standards: Initial reviews must be completed within 21 days. Reconsideration decisions must be issued within 21 days. Final reviews must be completed within 45 days. State MCSAP Lead Agencies must submit DataQs Implementation Plans detailing how they will meet the new requirements, address backlogs, and prevent future delays. To promote transparency, all approved plans will be publicly available through the DataQs system. Additional Information DataQs is FMCSA’s online system that allows drivers, motor carriers and other stakeholders to request a review of federal and state safety data they believe is incomplete, incorrect or inaccurate. The system provides a formal way to ask the government to review information and, when appropriate, correct it. All 50 states, Washington, D.C., and U.S. territories are compliant with the revised requirements. The updated framework establishes a consistent, multi-level review process, including clear timelines for responses, appeals and final decisions. Improving the DataQs process builds on the Trump Administration’s commitment to improving working conditions for America’s truck drivers and strengthening the commercial motor vehicle industry. ###

items.sourceText: Trump’s Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy Delivers $200 Million Truck Parking Expansion Across the Country in Major Win For American Truckers Wednesday, October 14, 2026 Funds will cover 14 expansion projects across 12 states to tackle truckers’ #1 problem when hauling critical cargo WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy today announced a $200 million investment to expand truck parking in 12 states through the Department’s Nationally Significant Multimodal Freight & Highway Projects (INFRA) program. These investments will expand public parking for hardworking truckers along America's most critical freight corridors and help reduce fatigue-related accidents, improve supply chain efficiency, and deliver significant savings. Reminder: 40% of truckers spend over an hour a day searching for parking—costing our national economy billions in wasted time. Limited safe, public commercial vehicle parking is also a safety issue – forcing truckers to park in harm's way. “American truckers are finally getting the attention and support they deserve thanks to President Trump,” said U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy . “These patriotic men and women work hard to ensure our store shelves are stocked, our gas stations are fueled, and our packages are delivered. They shouldn’t have to spend over an hour looking for a safe place to rest at the end of the day. This nationwide investment will make America’s truckers safer, enhance our supply chains, and reduce freight costs.” The investments are going toward 14 truck parking projects in 12 states, including: $11.95 million to the Georgia Ports Authority to build the Port of Savannah Commercial Motor Vehicle Parking Area adjacent to Georgia State Route 21 in Garden City, Georgia. This facility will have approximately 275 commercial vehicle spaces. $24.5 million to the Iowa Department of Transportation to expand and modernize commercial motor vehicle parking at six public rest areas along I-80 in Mitchellville, Wilton, Victor, Minden, and Underwood. $6 million to the North Carolina State Ports Authority to construct approximately 140 dedicated commercial motor vehicle parking spaces and approximately 50 container staging positions at the Port of Wilmington in New Hanover County, North Carolina. $5 million to the City of Fort Worth to construct approximately 100 new commercial motor vehicle parking spaces at the Pilot Travel Center in Fort Worth, Texas, along I-35. $9 million to Cameron County, Texas, to reconstruct approximately 0.35 miles of Rio Grande Avenue to provide access to a new public commercial motor vehicle parking facility near the Los Indios Port of Entry that will include approximately 305 dedicated truck parking spaces. $15 million to the Wisconsin Department of Transportation to expand commercial motor vehicle parking by approximately 106 spaces between two safety rest areas along a rural area of I-41 in Dodge County, Wisconsin.’ “Truck parking is one of the most persistent challenges faced by American truckers today, and under President Trump and Secretary Duffy, we’re tackling it head on,” said Federal Motor Carrier Administrator Derek D. Barrs . “This investment will deliver hundreds of new spots across the country, helping hardworking truck drivers get the rest they need and reducing dangerous roadside parking on some of America’s most important corridors.” These investments were made via the INFRA program, which bolsters America’s supply chains and improves road safety for families by building highways, bridges, and port infrastructure nationwide. See the full list of awards HERE . Additional Information: The Trump Administration has delivered historic wins for the American trucker in its effort to make American roads safe again. Since April 2025, USDOT has invested more than $300 million in truck parking grants. In July 2026, the Administration delivered an additional $62 million to address the truck parking shortage in Kentucky, Wyoming, Louisiana, Mississippi, and Illinois via the Better Utilizing Investments to Leverage Development (BUILD) grant program. ###

items.title: FMCSA Extends Automatic Relief Period for Regional Emergency Declarations
items.summary: Today, the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA) announced a final rule amending its emergency declaration regulations. The final rule revises the length of regulatory relief automatically triggered by a regional declaration of emergency, extending it from 14 days to 30 days.
items.sourceText: FMCSA Extends Automatic Relief Period for Regional Emergency Declarations Monday, October 5, 2026 INFORMATION BULLETIN Contact: FMCSA.PublicAffairs@dot.gov WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA) announced a final rule amending its emergency declaration regulations. The final rule revises the length of regulatory relief automatically triggered by a regional declaration of emergency, extending it from 14 days to 30 days. This automatic regulatory relief is enacted when a regional emergency is formally declared by a State Governor, a Governor's authorized representative, or FMCSA. By extending the automatic exemption to 30 days, FMCSA expects to significantly reduce the administrative burdens of filing and processing extension requests that were created by the previous 14-day limitation. This update also reflects a commitment to give states greater control over disaster response and trusting state leaders to know what's best for their state in the wake of emergencies. Key details regarding the final rule include: Effective Date: The final rule goes into effect immediately on October 5, 2026. Relief Extension: The rule extends the length of automatic regulatory relief from 14 days to 30 days. Triggering Entities: This automatic relief is triggered following a regional emergency declaration issued by a State Governor, a Governor's authorized representative, or FMCSA. For more information and to read the complete regulatory text, please see the Final Rule here .

items.sourceText: OPERATION SATURDAY NIGHT FEVER: Trump’s Transportation Department Joins Multi-State Operation, Removes More than 75 Unqualified Truckers from U.S. Roads Wednesday, September 30, 2026 FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE Contact: FMCSA.PublicAffairs@dot.gov Operation conducted 552 inspections that placed 78 drivers and 25 vehicles out of service COLUMBIA, SC — The U.S. Department of Transportation's Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA) participated in ‘Operation Saturday Night Fever,’ a coordinated, overnight commercial motor vehicle enforcement initiative focused on improving roadway safety and addressing criminal activity along major freight corridors. The operation took place on U.S. highways across South Carolina, North Carolina, Florida, and Georgia, and targeted unsafe drivers, hazardous vehicles, and violations that put motorists at risk. FMCSA Safety Investigators worked alongside the Department of Homeland Security and state police to conduct inspections, verify driver credentials, check for fatigue, evaluate electronic logging devices, look for distracted driving or unsecure cargo, and assess English Language Proficiency (ELP). The operation resulted in: 552 inspections 78 drivers placed out of service (including 12 for ELP violations), including drivers with non-domiciled commercial driver licenses (CDLs) 25 vehicles placed out of service “This operation reflects the strength of our law enforcement partnerships and our shared responsibility to keep America’s roads safe,” said FMCSA Administrator Derek D. Barrs . “By working together and focusing our enforcement, we can identify unsafe drivers and vehicles, disrupt criminal activity, and protect the integrity of our transportation system. Our message is simple: safety comes first, and those who put the public at risk will be held accountable.” “On behalf of the South Carolina State Transport Police and South Carolina Department of Public Safety, we are grateful for the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration’s support of the South Carolina State Transport Police’s Operation Saturday Night Fever, a periodic nighttime enforcement effort focused on commercial motor vehicle safety in high-crash corridors,” said South Carolina State Transport Police Colonel Dwayne Wilson . “Late evening and early morning hours are often when dangerous driving behaviors go unnoticed, and collisions can have serious — even deadly — consequences. Our goal, as always, is to reduce crashes while keeping trucks safely moving, recognizing that commercial vehicles are vital to South Carolina’s supply chain and to our nation’s economy.” “This enforcement initiative showcases North Carolina’s continued commitment to working alongside local, state and federal agencies in the pursuit of saving lives on our roadways,” said North Carolina State Highway Patrol Commander Colonel Freddy L. Johnson, Jr. “Combining resources, sharing ideas and working in consort with law enforcement partners to promote the safe operation of commercial motor vehicles is not just practical, but indispensable in furthering our ongoing educational and enforcement efforts." “At the Florida Highway Patrol, we are proud to once again work alongside our law enforcement and public safety partners in combatting illegal, unsafe driving practices and taking unfit drivers out of service,” said Florida Highway Patrol Colonel Gary Howze. “Our Commercial Vehicle Enforcement Troopers lead the way in keeping Florida’s roadways safe, enforcing rigorous standards that hold commercial drivers accountable and safeguard everyone who travels through our state.” “Unsafe carriers do not stop at state lines, and neither should our partnerships,” said Georgia Department of Public Safety, Commercial Vehicle Enforcement (CVE) Major Andrew Montgomery. “Operation Saturday Night Fever put those partnerships into action along the I-95 corridor. By working together across state lines, our agencies can share information, focus resources where they are needed most, and take action when we find serious safety issues. The overwhelming majority of professional drivers take their responsibilities seriously every day. Our goal is to hold the bad actors accountable, protect everyone who shares the highway, and allow the drivers and carriers who follow the rules to keep freight moving safely.” Additional Information: ‘Operation Saturday Night Fever’ was conducted Saturday, September 26. Since President Trump issued an Executive Order to restore integrity to the trucking industry in April 2025, Secretary Duffy and FMCSA have: Placed 31,200 drivers out of service who could not speak basic English or read road signs; Shut down nearly 10,000 driving schools; and Revoked more than 31,000 illegally issued licenses to unvetted foreign drivers. ### Under U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy, the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA) is dedicated to reducing crashes, fatalities and injuries involving large trucks and buses. FMCSA oversees the safety of the nation’s 9 million commercial motor vehicle drivers and ensures compliance across the trucking industry that serves as the backbone of the American economy. Visit FMCSA.dot.gov for more information.
